answer: What weather conditions are commonly associated with a cold front?
reference_answer: Prior to and during the passage of a cold front, towering cumulus or cumulonimbus clouds dominate the sky, frequently producing heavy rain showers, lightning, thunder, gusty winds, and poor visibility [phak-ch12 p.12-20]. More severe cold fronts can generate sudden storms, turbulence, hail, and even tornadoes along the frontal boundary, while temperatures and dew points drop rapidly during passage [phak-ch12 p.12-20] [phak-ch12 p.12-21]. Barometric pressure falls quickly as the front approaches, bottoms out during frontal passage, and then begins a gradual increase [phak-ch12 p.12-20]. After the front passes, the clouds dissipate, precipitation decreases, and cooler, drier air prevails with rapidly clearing skies and good visibility [phak-ch12 p.12-20] [phak-ch12 p.12-21].
